newsitem.title: FRENCH GUIANA: Textbook Ariane launches for PanAmSat satellite.
newsitem.headline: Textbook Ariane launches for PanAmSat satellite.

text.p: Western Europe's 98th Ariane rocket put a communications satellite for global satellite operator PanAmSat into orbit after a textbook launch from equatorial French Guiana early on Friday.
The Ariane 44P rocket lifted off at 3.46 a.m. local time (0646 GMT) from the European Space Agency (ESA) launch centre in Kourou, French Guiana on the northeast coast of South America.
Space officials said the PanAmSat-6 (PAS-6) satellite separated from the Ariane rocket 21 minutes after lift-off.

PAS-6 will provide direct television broadcasting to South America for a consortium of the media companies News Corporation, Grupo Televisa, Organizacoes Globo and Tele-Communications International, PanAmSat chairman Fred Landman told a pre-launch news conference.
"DTH (direct-to-home service) is playing an increasing large role in the delivery of entertainment and information to the public at large on a cost effective basis," he said.

Landman said the cost of PAS-6 -- satellite, launch and insurance -- was in excess of $225 million. PanAmSat and Hughes Electronics, a division of General Motors, merged in May to create a network of 15 telecommunications satellites.
The company plans to launch a 16th satellite later this month aboard a Russian Proton rocket and have a fleet of 21 satellites in operation by the end of 1998.

PAS-6, which is due to operate for the next 22 years, weighs 3.4 tonnes and was built in the U.S. by Space Systems/Loral. It is designed to transmit 360 digital television channels that can be received using dishes as small a 60 centimeters.
Arianespace has placed 23 satellites aboard 15 Ariane-4 rockets since January 1996. The company says it has firm orders to launch 43 heavy satellites worth about $3.4 billion.
But in June 1996, the first more powerful, new generation Ariane-5 rocket exploded 37 seconds after its maiden launch in a major setback for the European space programme.

Arianespace was scheduled to take over operations of Ariane-5 early this year. The new rocket's commercial future is now in doubt and a second experimental launch of the more powerful rocket is planned for late September at earliest.
